event.sentence: Limit each signed-in user to ten requests per 60 seconds on the link API, counting failed requests too, and answer over-limit requests with 429.

tasks.brief: In ratelimit machine implement per-user fixed-window limiter: keyed by signed-in user ID, allow 10 requests per 60 seconds. Expose consume/check(userId) returning allowed boolean plus remaining and reset/retry seconds. Increment on every call including failed requests - caller will call before handler. Store counters with 60s expiry and auto-reset, using in-memory map or store machine. No HTTP status handling here.
tasks.title: Rate limiter core

tasks.brief: Wire limiting into the link API: in middleware/server extract signed-in user ID via auth, call ratelimit consume on every link API request in links/server before handler so failed requests still count. If over limit, short-circuit with HTTP 429 response via errors machine including Retry-After header. Apply only to link API routes and only to authenticated users; unauthenticated bypasses.
tasks.title: Enforce limit on links

tasks.brief: In test machine add coverage for link API rate limiting: authenticated user can make 10 requests per 60s then 11th gets 429; bucket resets after 60s; failed/bad requests still count toward the 10; different users have independent buckets. Mock time or limiter store to avoid real 60s waits. Exercise via links endpoints through middleware/server.
tasks.title: Rate limit coverage

event.sentence: Send a Retry-After header on every 429 response, in whole seconds rounded up.

tasks.brief: In the main rate-limit path, send Retry-After on every 429 response in whole seconds rounded up (ceil). Update ratelimit logic (using store timing as needed) to compute seconds_until_allowed = ceil(ms_until_reset / 1000) with minimum 1, and set `Retry-After: <seconds>` on the 429 response. Examples: 100ms -> 1, 1000ms -> 1, 1500ms -> 2, 2000ms -> 2. Expose the reset delay to middleware if needed so the header is set. Do not change limits or response bodies, only add the header.
tasks.title: Rate limiter Retry-After

tasks.brief: Guarantee every 429 response sent by the server carries a Retry-After header in whole seconds rounded up. In server / middleware / errors response handling, add a final safeguard: if status is 429 and Retry-After is missing or not a whole-second integer, set it to ceil(known retry delay / 1000) with minimum 1, defaulting to 1 if no delay info is available. Ensure errors formatting and server helpers preserve and pass through the header. This covers all 429 sources beyond the main limiter.
tasks.title: Guarantee header on all 429s

tasks.brief: Ensure auth-related 429s (login throttling, brute-force lockout) send Retry-After in whole seconds rounded up. In auth logic, when returning 429 compute remaining lockout/throttle time as ceil(ms_remaining / 1000) with minimum 1 and set `Retry-After: <seconds>` header. If auth uses the shared limiter pass through its delay; if it has its own counters compute locally. Do not change auth allow/deny decisions, only add the header.
tasks.title: Auth throttle Retry-After
